public_title: How Mammal Play Signals Pure Joy 🐒
hook: You feel a sudden urge to roughhouse with your pet.

sections.title: Story
sections.narration: You feel a sudden urge to roughhouse with your pet. Ancient thinkers actually saw this play as a vital brain signal for survival and joy. In 1998, neuroscientist Jaak Panksepp studied laboratory rats in Bowling Green and measured over 500 ultrasonic laughs per hour during play. What did the researchers find? The animals produced distinct vocalizations only when engaged in social games. It was not just one species. Later studies on wild chimpanzees in Tanzania revealed identical joy signals during daily play. Science calls this the mammalian play circuit. So why do we assume animal play is just random energy? Evolutionary biology shows it actively builds social bonds and reduces stress. The result? Joy is an ancient survival tool hardwired into your nervous system. That's it. So next time you play with a dog, remember you feel a sudden urge to roughhouse with your pet.

claims.claim: Rats produce ultrasonic vocalizations (laughter) during play, measuring over 500 calls per hour.
Chimpanzees display distinct play faces and vocal signals during social play that mirror human laughter.

theme: How Animals Show Joy Through Play
